questions.question: A sum of money became Rs. 2,700 in two years. If the simple interest offered per annum was 2% more, the amount would have become Rs. 2,800 during the same period. Find the originals sum and the rate of simple interest offered every year.
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

SI = (P × R × T)/100

SI = Amount - Principle

**Calculation:**

Let the original sum be x and rate be r

Difference in SI for 2 years = 2800 - 2700 = 100

SI₂ - SI₁ = (P₂ × R₂ × T₂)/100 - (P₁ × R₁ × T₁)/100

⇒ 2800 - 2700 = (x × 2 × (R₂ - R₁))/100

⇒ 100 × 100 = (x × 2 × 2)

⇒ x = 2500

Now, SI = Amount - Principle

⇒ 2700 - 2500 = 200

Time = 2 years and Rate = r %

SI = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ 200 = (2500 × r × 2)/100

⇒ r = (200 × 100)/5000

⇒ r = 4 %

**∴ Original sum is Rs 2500 and Rate is 4 %**

questions.question: What is the region called where rivers deposit pebbles in a narrow belt near the Shiwaliks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhabar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhabar** region is a narrow belt of land located at the foothills of the **Shiwalik Hills** in the Himalayas.
 
• It is characterized by the deposition of **coarse sediments, such as pebbles and gravel**, brought down by rivers flowing from the Himalayas.
 
• These sediments are deposited in a narrow strip because the rivers lose their velocity upon reaching the plains.
 
• Due to the porous nature of the soil in the Bhabar region, most of the rivers disappear or percolate into the ground, creating an underground water table.
 
• The Bhabar belt is generally devoid of surface water and is unsuitable for agriculture because of its rocky and coarse texture.
 
• This region lies to the north of the **Terai** belt and acts as a transition zone between the mountains and the plains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Delta**__

 __
 
• A **delta** is a landform created by the deposition of sediments at the mouth of a river where it meets a standing body of water, such as a sea or an ocean.
 
• Examples include the **Sundarbans Delta** formed by the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers.
 
• Deltas are usually fertile and support extensive agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Plateau**__
 __
 
• A **plateau** is an elevated flatland that stands significantly above the surrounding area.
 
• Examples include the **Deccan Plateau** in India.
 
• Plateaus are rich in minerals and often support mining activities.
 
 
 
• **Terai**__
 
 
• The **Terai** is a fertile, marshy region lying south of the Bhabar belt.
 
• It is characterized by the presence of surface water and dense vegetation due to the rivers re-emerging from the ground.
 
• The Terai region is highly suitable for agriculture and supports crops like rice and sugarcane.

questions.question: Five years ago, the age of Bali and Geeta was in the ratio 3 : 4 respectively. After ten years, the ratio of their ages will be 6 : 7 respectively. What is the difference in their present age?

The ratio of their (Bali and Gita) age 5 years ago = 3 : 4

**Calculation:**

Let the age of Gita and Bali before 5 years be 4x and 3x respectively

According to the question

⇒ 21x + 105 = 24x + 90

⇒ 24x - 21x = 105 - 90

⇒ 3x = 15

⇒ x = 5

The age of Bali before 5 years = 3x = 5 × 3 = 15

The present age of Bali = 15 + 5 = 20

The age of Gita before 5 years = 4x = 4 × 5 = 20

The present age of Gita = 20 + 5 = 25

The difference of their present age = 25 - 20 = 5 years

**∴ The required result will be 5 years.**

questions.question: When a Judge of a High Court in India, including the Chief Justice, wishes to resign from office, to whom must they submit their resignation?

options.text: The Governor of the respective state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Judge of a High Court in India, including the Chief Justice, submits their resignation to **The President of India**.
 
• The resignation must be in writing, addressed formally to the President, as per **Article 217(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The process ensures accountability and adherence to constitutional protocols regarding judicial appointments and resignations.
 
• High Court Judges hold office until the age of 62 years or until resignation, removal, or transfer as per constitutional provisions.
 
• The President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers while accepting the resignation of a High Court Judge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 217 of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• It deals with the appointment and conditions of service of High Court Judges.
 
• It specifies the qualifications for becoming a High Court Judge, including being a citizen of India and having at least 10 years of judicial experience.
 
• It covers provisions related to resignation, removal, and transfer of High Court Judges.
 
 
 
• **Removal of High Court Judges**
 
 
• Judges can be removed through a process called impeachment, as per **Article 124(4)** and **Article 217(1)(b)**.
 
• The process requires a majority vote in Parliament based on proven misconduct or incapacity.
 
 
 
• **Transfer of High Court Judges**
 
 
• Under **Article 222**, the President has the power to transfer a High Court Judge after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
 
• Transfers are made to ensure better administration of justice or to fill vacancies in other High Courts.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Chief Justice of India (CJI)**
 
 
• The CJI plays a crucial advisory role in matters related to the appointment, transfer, and removal of High Court Judges.
 
• This ensures a transparent and balanced approach to judicial administration.

questions.question: In a ΔABC, if ∠A = 90°, AC = 5 cm, BC = 9 cm, and in ΔPQR, ∠P = 90°, PR = 3 cm, QR = 8 cm, then:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Compare corresponding parts of right-angled ΔABC and ΔPQR.

In ΔABC: Hypotenuse BC = 9 cm and Side AC = 5 cm.

In ΔPQR: Hypotenuse QR = 8 cm and Side PR = 3 cm.

Congruence (RHS) requires Hypotenuse 1 = Hypotenuse 2 and Side 1 = Side 2.

Since 9 ≠ 8 and 5 ≠ 3, the triangles cannot be congruent.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≇ ΔPQR.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC: ∠A = 90°, AC = 5 cm, BC = 9 cm (Hypotenuse)

ΔPQR: ∠P = 90°, PR = 3 cm, QR = 8 cm (Hypotenuse)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89b0ac819db213682b3bf2149aa361401a41fe3ddac32e59e458778a5e09dee8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) Congruence Rule: Two right-angled triangles are congruent if the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and the corresponding side of the other triangle.

⇒ In ΔABC, using Pythagoras theorem: AB² = BC² − AC²

⇒ AB² = 9² − 5² = 81 − 25 = 56
⇒ AB = √56 cm ≈ 7.48 cm

⇒ In ΔPQR, using Pythagoras theorem: PQ² = QR² − PR²

⇒ PQ² = 8² − 3² = 64 − 9 = 55
⇒ PQ = √55 cm ≈ 7.41 cm

⇒ Comparing the dimensions of ΔABC and ΔPQR:

⇒ Hypotenuse: BC (9 cm) ≠ QR (8 cm)
⇒ Side 1: AC (5 cm) ≠ PR (3 cm)
⇒ Side 2: AB (√56 cm) ≠ PQ (√55 cm)

⇒ Since none of the corresponding sides are equal, the triangles are not congruent.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≇ ΔPQR.**

**__Additional Information__**

RHS Congruence Rule

If in two right-angled triangles, the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one side of the other triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.

SSS Congruence Rule

Two triangles are congruent if all three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding three sides of the other triangle.

Congruence vs. Equality

Congruent triangles (≅) have the exact same shape and size (identical sides and angles), whereas equal triangles (=) usually refers to triangles having equal area even if shapes differ.</p

questions.question: If the number 6523678pq is divisible by 99, the missing digits p and q are :
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number 6523678pq is divisible by 99.

**Concept used:**

Divisibility rule of 9 ⇒ for any number to be divisible by 9, the sum of its digit should be divisible by 9.

Divisibility rule of 11 ⇒ the subtraction of alternate digits of the number should add up to zero or be divisible by 11.

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

6523678pq is divisible by 99

This means it is divisible by (11 × 9)

∴ It is divisible by both 11 and 9

Divisibility by 9,

⇒ (6 + 5 + 2 + 3 + 6 + 7 + 8 + p + q) should be divisible by 9

⇒ (37 + p + q) is divisible by 9 

⇒ p + q = 8 .....(1) [ The nearest multiple of 9 greater than 37 is 45. Hence we have to add 8 to the 37 to make it a multiple of 9]

Divisibility by 11,

⇒ (6 + 2 + 6 + 8 + q) - (5 + 3 + 7 + p) = 11

⇒ 22 + q - 15 - p = 11

⇒ q - p = 11 - 7 = 4 .....(2)

Adding (1) and (2), we get

⇒ 2 × q = 12 ⇒ q = 6

p = 8 - q = 8 - 6

⇒ p = 2

**∴ The value of p = 2 and q = 6.**

__
 
• A **Linker** is classified as a system software, not an application software.
 
• System software like Linker is used to manage and control computer hardware and serves as a platform for other software.
 
• The primary function of a Linker is to combine multiple object files (produced by the compiler) into a single executable file.
 
• Application software, on the other hand, includes programs designed for end-users, such as spreadsheets (e.g., MS Excel), presentation tools (e.g., MS PowerPoint), and design software (e.g., AutoCAD).

• Examples include MS PowerPoint, MS Excel, AutoCAD, web browsers, and media players.
 
• Application software is user-oriented and directly interacts with the end-user.
 
 
 
• **System Software:**
 
 
• System software acts as an intermediary between hardware and application software.
 
• Examples include operating systems (e.g., Windows, Linux), compilers, and linkers.
 
• System software is primarily designed for managing system resources and enabling the functionality of application software.
 
 
 
• **Linker:**
 
 
• A linker is a system software tool used in programming to combine object files into a single executable file.
 
• It resolves references between different modules and ensures the program runs correctly.
 
• Linkers are a critical part of the software development process, typically used in languages like C, C++, and assembly.
 
 
 
• **Compiler:**
 
 
• A compiler is another system software used to translate high-level programming code into machine code.
 
• It works alongside the linker to create executable programs.
 
• While compilers convert source code into object code, linkers bring together multiple object code files.

The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the Constitution of India,** Article 32** provides for the right to constitutional remedies, while **Article 226** empowers High Courts to issue writs. The following are the different types of writs that can be issued under these articles:

 
 
• **Habeas corpus - to produce a person who is under illegal detention**
 
• **Mandamus - to compel a public official or body to perform a duty**
 
• **Prohibition - to prohibit a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction**
 
• **Certiorari - to quash the order of a lower court or tribunal**
 
• **Quo warranto - to question the authority or legality of a person holding a public office**
 
 
 
• Thus, a total of five types of writs can be issued under **Article 32 and 226** of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the** right to constitutional remedies to every citizen of India**.

 
 
• This article empowers the citizens to approach the Supreme Court of India to seek enforcement of their **fundamental rights.**
 
• The** Supreme Court** has the power to issue** writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto,** for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.
 
• The right to move th**e Supreme Court under Article 32 **is considered as a fundamental right in itself, and any law or action that violates the fundamental rights can be challenged under this article.
 
• This article ensures that the citizens have a direct access to the **Supreme Court**, which is the highest court of** the land, to seek justice and protection of their rights.**
 
• **Article 32** is often regarded as the most important and valuable provision in the Indian Constitution, as it provides a powerful mechanism to protect the fundamental rights of the citizens and to ensure that the government acts in accordance with the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 226 of the Constitution of India empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.**
 
 
• The High Court, being the highest court in a state, has wide-ranging powers to exercise judicial review over the decisions of inferior courts, tribunals, and other authorities within its territorial jurisdiction.

questions.question: The last stage of demographic transition model is characterized by____.

options.text: Low Birth Rate and High Death Rate
Low Birth Rate and Low Death Rate
High Birth Rate and Low Death Rate
High Birth Rate and High Death Rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low Birth Rate and Low Death Rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The last stage of the demographic transition model is known as the **Post-Industrial Stage**.
 
• It is characterized by both **low birth rates and low death rates**, leading to a stabilized population.
 
• Factors such as increased access to education, healthcare, and family planning are significant contributors to the decline in birth rates.
 
• Death rates remain low due to **advancements in medical technologies** and improved living standards.
 
• This stage is typical in **developed countries** where economic development and societal changes have reached maturity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demographic Transition Model (DTM):**

 
 
• A model that describes population change over time as a country develops economically.
 
• It has four stages: Pre-Industrial, Transitional, Industrial, and Post-Industrial.
 
 
 
• **Birth Rate:** The number of live births per 1,000 people in a year. It decreases in the final stage of the demographic transition due to social and economic changes.
 
• **Death Rate:** The number of deaths per 1,000 people in a year. It remains low in the last stage due to advancements in healthcare and improved living standards.
 
• **Population Stabilization:** In the post-industrial stage, the population size stabilizes as both birth and death rates are low and balanced.
 
• **Examples of Countries in the Last Stage:** Developed countries like Germany, Japan, and Sweden are in this stage of demographic transition.

questions.question: Which type of soil is found in maximum quantity in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial soil** is the most widespread type of soil in India, covering approximately **43% of the total land area**. It is predominantly found in the northern plains and river valleys.
 
• It is formed by the deposition of **sediments brought by rivers**, mainly the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus rivers. The soil is highly fertile and suitable for agriculture.
 
• The soil is rich in **potassium, phosphoric acid, and lime**, making it ideal for the cultivation of crops like **rice, wheat, sugarcane, and pulses**. It also supports horticultural crops.
 
• Alluvial soil is divided into two types: **Khadar** (new alluvium) and **Bhangar** (old alluvium). Khadar soil is more fertile and found in floodplains, while Bhangar soil is coarse and found in higher regions.
 
• This soil is mainly found in states like **Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam**, along with parts of Gujarat and Rajasthan.
 
• Alluvial soils are also characterized by their **loamy texture**, which provides good drainage and aeration for crops. However, they may lack nitrogen and organic matter, which can be supplemented through fertilizers.
 
• Due to their high fertility, alluvial soils play a critical role in supporting India's **agricultural economy**, contributing to food security and economic development.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Alluvial soil.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Red Soil:**

 
 
• **Red soil** derives its red color from the presence of **iron oxide**. It is found in regions like Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha.
 
• It is less fertile compared to alluvial soil but supports crops like **millets, pulses, and groundnuts**. Fertilizers and organic matter are required to enhance its productivity.
 
 
 
• **Black Soil:**
 
 
• **Black soil**, also known as **Regur soil** or cotton soil, is found in regions like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is rich in **calcium carbonate, magnesium, and potash**, making it ideal for crops like **cotton, sugarcane, and pulses**. However, it has poor drainage and develops cracks during dry seasons.
 
 
 
• **Velvet Soil:**
 
 
• There is no recognized type of soil called **Velvet soil**. This option is incorrect and does not exist in soil classification.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Distribution:**

 
 
• India's northern plains are extensively covered with **alluvial soil**, deposited by rivers originating from the Himalayas.
 
• It is also found in coastal regions and deltas, including the Sundarbans in West Bengal and the Mahanadi delta in Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Soil Classification in India:**
 
 
• India has a diverse range of soils, including **alluvial soil, red soil, black soil, laterite soil, desert soil, and mountain soil**, each supporting specific agricultural practices.
 
• The **National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning (NBSS&LUP)** conducts soil research and classification to optimize land use and agricultural productivity.

• It was founded in September 1932 in the wake of Gandhiji's Epic Fast at Yervada Jail, Pune, resulting in the historic Poona Pact.
 
• The immediate historical background dates back to the Second Round Table Conference in London in 1931 when Gandhi Ji opposed the segregation of the depressed classes of the Hindu community into a separate electoral group.
 
• Gandhi Ji saw in it a sinister device of the British government to create a split in the Hindu community in furtherance of its policy of divide and rule.

questions.question: P alone can complete a work in 15 days and Q alone can complete the same work in 12 days. They start the work together but after 3 days P leaves the work. How much time will Q take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(15, 12) = 60 units.

Efficiency of P = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units/day | Efficiency of Q = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units/day.

Work done together in 3 days = 3 × (4 + 5) = 27 units.

Remaining time for Q = (60 − 27) ÷ 5 = 33 ÷ 5 = 6.6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 15 days.

Time taken by Q to complete the work = 12 days.

P and Q work together for 3 days, then P leaves.

**Method Used:**

LCM Method: Total Work = LCM of individual days.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P
 15
 60

 Q
 12
 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = 60 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P and Q = 4 + 5 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by P and Q in 3 days = 9 × 3 = 27 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 27 = 33 units.

⇒ Time taken by Q to finish the remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Q's efficiency.

⇒ Time taken by Q = 33 ÷ 5 = 6.6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fractional Work Method

If a person completes a job in x days, then the part of the work completed in 1 day is 1/x. Work remaining after n days is 1 − (n ÷ x).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by the individuals. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept of time and work directly applies to pipes and cisterns. Filling a tank is considered positive work, while emptying a tank is considered negative work.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that 'there shall be a Vice President of India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 63**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Article 63**

 
 
• Article 63 of the Indian Constitution states that "There shall be a vice president of India."
 
 
• The vice president acts as president in the absence of the president due to death, resignation, impeachment, or other situations.
 
 
 
• The vice president of India is also ex officio chairperson of the Rajya Sabha. When a bill is introduced in Rajya Sabha, the vice president decides whether it is a financial bill or not.
 
 
• If he is of the opinion, a bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha is a money bill, he would refer the case to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha for deciding it.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 61**
 
• The process for the impeachment of the President is outlined in Article 61 of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
• Either House of Parliament may file the impeachment accusations.
 
• The President must be notified 14 days in advance, and these allegations must be signed by one-fourth of the House members who framed them.
 
• The other House, which is tasked with conducting an investigation into the allegations, receives the impeachment resolution when it has been approved by a two-thirds majority of the entire membership of that House.
 
• The President has the right to show up and be represented during such an investigation.
 
• The President is removed from office as of the date the resolution is passed if the other House concurs with the accusations and approves the impeachment resolution with a two-thirds majority of its members.
 
• Impeachment is a quasi-judicial process in Parliament as a result.
 
 
 
• In this context, it is important to keep in mind two things:
 
 
• nominated members of either House of Parliament may take part in the impeachment of the President even though they did not cast a ballot in his election;
 
• and elected members of state legislative assemblies and the union territories of Delhi and Puducherry may not, even though they cast a ballot in the President's election.
 
 
 
• **Article 65**
 
 
• Article 65 deals with the Vice-President acting as President or discharging the functions of the President in the event of a vacancy.
 
 
 
• ​Article 62
 
 
• **Article 62 **of the Indian Constitution deals with the time frame for holding an election to fill a vacancy in the office of the **President.**

questions.question: ​A person with 30 km/h reaches Dharmatala to Eden Garden in 30 minutes. If he has to reach the distance in 20 minutes, then what will be his speed (in km/h) ?

He travels the distance in 30 minutes.

Speed (S) = Distance (D) / Time (T)

**Calculation**:

Speed = 30 km/h

So in 30 minutes, he travels (1 / 2) × 30 = 15 km

So, the distance is 15 km

Now, in 20 minutes he has to travel 15 km

So, in 60 minutes he will travel ((15)/(20)) × 60 = 15 × 3

⇒ 45 km/h 

**His speed will be 45 km/h**

value of 2x = 30

⇒ x = 15

Then, value of 3x = 3 × 15

⇒ 45

His speed will be 45 km/h

questions.question: The profit earned on selling an article for Rs. 4550 is 5 times of the loss incurred on selling the same article for Rs. 3290. What will be the selling price of the article to earn a profit of 20 percent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price for profit = Rs. 4550

Selling price for loss = Rs. 3290

Profit earned is 5 times the loss

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price

Loss = Cost Price - Selling Price

Profit = 5 × Loss

Selling Price for 20% profit = Cost Price × (1 + Profit Percentage)

**Calculation:**

Let Cost Price be CP.

Profit when selling at Rs. 4550:

Profit = 4550 - CP

Loss when selling at Rs. 3290:

Loss = CP - 3290

Given, Profit = 5 × Loss

⇒ 4550 - CP = 5 × (CP - 3290)

⇒ 4550 - CP = 5CP - 16450

⇒ 4550 + 16450 = 6CP

⇒ 21000 = 6CP

⇒ CP = 21000 / 6

⇒ CP = 3500

Selling Price for 20% profit:

SP = CP × (1 + 20/100)

SP = 3500 × 1.2

SP = 4200

**The selling price of the article to earn a profit of 20 percent is Rs. 4200.**

questions.question: dfrac{5sqrt{5}x³ - 81sqrt{3}y³}{sqrt{5}x - 3sqrt{3}y} = Ax² + By² + Cxy, then find the value of 16A + B - sqrt{15}C?

**Given:**

**dfrac{5sqrt{5}x³ - 81sqrt{3}y³}{sqrt{5}x - 3sqrt{3}y} **= Ax2 + By2 + Cxy

**Formula used:**

a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + b² + ab)

**Calculation:**

dfrac{5sqrt{5}x³ - 81sqrt{3}y³}{sqrt{5}x - 3sqrt{3}y} = Ax2 + By2 + Cxy

⇒ dfrac{(sqrt{5}x)³ - (3sqrt{3}y)³}{sqrt{5}x - 3sqrt{3}y} = Ax2 + By2 + Cxy

⇒ dfrac{(sqrt{5}x - 3sqrt{3}y)[(sqrt{5}x)² + (3sqrt{3}y)² + sqrt{5}x × 3sqrt{3}y]}{sqrt{5}x - 3sqrt{3}y} = Ax2 + By2 + Cxy

⇒ {[(sqrt{5}x)² + (3sqrt{3}y)² + sqrt{5}x × 3sqrt{3}y]} = Ax2 + By2 + Cxy

⇒ 5x² + 27y² + 3sqrt{15}xy = Ax2 + By2 + Cxy

Hence, A = 5, B = 27 and C = 3sqrt{15}

Now, 16A + B - sqrt{15}C

⇒ 16 × 5 + 27 - sqrt{15} × 3sqrt{15}

**∴ 16A + B - sqrt{15} C = 62**

questions.question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 146 cm and one of its diagonals is 55 cm. Find the area of the rhombus.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Perimeter of the rhombus = 146 cm

One of the diagonals = 55 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a rhombus = 4 × side length

Area of a rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

**Calculation:**

Let the side length of the rhombus be a cm.

Perimeter = 4a

4a = 146

⇒ a = 146 / 4

⇒ a = 36.5 cm

Let the diagonals be d₁ and d₂, where d₁ = 55 cm.

Using Pythagoras theorem in one of the right triangles formed by the diagonals:

(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)² = a²

(55/2)² + (d₂/2)² = 36.5²

⇒ (27.5)² + (d₂/2)² = 36.5²

⇒ 756.25 + (d₂/2)² = 1332.25

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 1332.25 - 756.25

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 576

⇒ (d₂/2) = √576

⇒ (d₂/2) = 24

⇒ d₂ = 24 × 2

⇒ d₂ = 48 cm

Area of the rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

Area = (1/2) × 55 × 48

Area = 1320 cm²

**The correct answer is option 3: 1320 cm²**

questions.question: In which season Kharif and Rabi Crops are grown respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rainy, winter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kharif crops** are sown during the beginning of the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in the rainy season (September-October).
 
• **Rabi crops** are sown at the beginning of the winter season (October-November) and harvested during summer (March-April).
 
• Kharif crops require high temperatures and abundant water supply, which is why they are grown during the rainy season.
 
• Rabi crops thrive in cold climates and require less water, making winter the ideal season for their growth.
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include rice, maize, and cotton, while examples of Rabi crops include wheat, mustard, and barley.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif crops:** Also known as monsoon crops, they are dependent on rainfall and are grown in regions with adequate monsoon patterns.
 
• **Rabi crops:** Known as winter crops, they rely on irrigation rather than rainfall, as they are grown in dry conditions.
 
• **Climatic conditions:** The success of Kharif crops depends on the timing and intensity of monsoon rains, while Rabi crops are sensitive to frost and require cool temperatures.
 
• **Double cropping:** In some regions, farmers grow both Kharif and Rabi crops in the same year, maximizing agricultural yield.
 
• **Economic significance:** These cropping patterns play a crucial role in India's agriculture-dependent economy by ensuring year-round food production.
